texts.text: Can't even tell if this is made from leather or fabric.
These old, tattered pairs of shoes won't take us anywhere.
A chaotic jumble of remnants. Le Noir branded clothes... furnishings...
A slide. It's so old and rusted that it might crumble if we tried to ride it.
There are papers on the table. One of them catches my eye.
[MISSING PERSON]
[Description: Burn scar on the face, scarf, leather bag...]
[Last Seen: Courthouse Sisyphe, Hall ■, Grand Auditorium]
<... This has to be describing Dubois, right?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... Courthouse Sisyphe is an ancient form of the Sisyphe System.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Unlike the things of eld, Dubois assumed a form that is generally accepted as human. If the individual this paper is describing truly is Dubois, I... fail to understand how this is possible.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <This might've just been a coincidence, but...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: <... Meursault, can experiences remain even when the memories of them have eroded away?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: ... I believe so, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: I don't know what to make of that.
I'll commit that to memory and revisit it later. Right now, making our way upstairs is our priority.
Don't think looking at it again will suddenly light the spark of inspiration in my head.
A pile of broken furnishings. All that time, and no one's purchased a single one of them.
Busily inspecting the fissure.
An expensive handbag, but it is empty inside.
The worth of a bag does not determine the value of what lies within, it seems.
The black couch—or what it looked like at first, at least—speaks to us.
... And here I was, surprised to see customers in the Furniture Hall again... I see that you are strangers.
texts.speaker: Couch?

texts.text: What happened to the other furnishings?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: They all met a predictable end. Concerned solely about making themselves more expensive, they failed to consider who, in their right mind, would purchase them.
texts.speaker: Couch?

texts.text: They refused to lower their standards even after the Rouges have stripped them of anything even remotely valuable, and... well, the results lay plainly before you.
texts.speaker: Couch?

texts.text: <... So you're the last survivor?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: The Manager would like to know if you are the sole survivor.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Oh yes, because I've chosen my buyer. And have had much to discuss with the sunshine, too.
texts.speaker: Couch?

texts.text: She has very high hopes for you, dear strangers.
texts.speaker: Couch?

texts.text: "She"... as in the sunshine? Are you talking about Miss Carmen?
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: Hm... The sunshine is indeed a warm and kind being... but it does not lead, nor does it promise us a tomorrow.
texts.speaker: Couch?

texts.text: The sunshine is no different from any other natural phenomenon. The sunshine is as much a sunshine as rain is rain.
texts.speaker: Couch?

texts.text: The Voice of Le Néant, on the other hand... has promised me a tomorrow.
texts.speaker: Couch?

texts.text: <... Le Néant.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: If you are weary, feel free to rest your feet awhile. Though I can't promise it'll be too comfortable.
texts.speaker: Couch?

texts.text: <No thanks.>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: No thank you.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: Then farewell. I look forward to your deconstruction of this department store.
texts.speaker: Couch?

texts.text: The black couch... Le Néant falls still again under the shadows, awaiting.
<Renée...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Ah... you've already made it this far.
texts.speaker: Renée

texts.text: It seems it won't be long before we can enjoy a little sunbathing.
texts.speaker: Renée

texts.text: <Carmen—I mean, the sunshine... what exactly does it want?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: We wish to know... what the sunshine wants.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: What a strange thing to ask. The sunshine... only wants what we want.
texts.speaker: Renée

texts.text: Even when the sunlight disagrees with us, so long as our wish, our emotion is sincere... it comes to want what we want.
texts.speaker: Renée

texts.text: <If that's the case, Meursault...>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Meursault had said that the sunshine was chatty. Irritatingly so.
Usually, those are the sort of words people use when something doesn't sit right with what they think...
... What the sunshine whispered to me was entirely congruent to what I wanted, Manager.
texts.speaker: Meursault

texts.text: <Then... what makes it so irritating?>
texts.speaker: Dante

texts.text: Meursault fell silent, sinking deeper into thought as if he could no longer bring himself to continue.
Almost as though something had frightened him.
Are you heading to 5F?
texts.speaker: Renée

texts.text: Yes. We need to climb higher.
texts.speaker: Hong Lu

texts.text: 5F... is where the Rouges have made themselves at home. That's where they are devouring the department store... bit by bit.
texts.speaker: Renée

texts.text: I do hope you'll make it past them... and find your way to the higher floors.
texts.speaker: Renée

texts.text: Soon, we will all return to our homes—save for the Crimson God.
texts.speaker: Le Néant

texts.text: We owe everything to you, strangers.
texts.speaker: Le Néant
